pedagogicalGoals: Understand why standard RNNs struggle with long-range dependencies
Master the intuition behind Query, Key, and Value vectors
Calculate Scaled Dot-Product Attention mathematically and implement in PyTorch

modules.title: The Query, Key, and Value Intuition
modules.teachingScript: <emotion=enthusiastic>Welcome to today's session! Aaj hum explore karne wale hain Transformer architecture ka sabse revolutionary component: Self-Attention Mechanism. <pause=300ms> Socho agar aap ek lamba sentence padh rahe ho, jaise 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired' - aapka dimaag turant samajh jata hai ki 'it' yahan animal ke liye hai, street ke liye nahi. Par computer yeh kaise samjhe? Let's visualize this on our smart whiteboard!</emotion>

visualAction.title: Self-Attention Information Flow
visualAction.rawPayload:
graph TD
    Input["Input Token Embeddings (X)"] --> Q["Query Matrix (Q = X * Wq)"]
    Input --> K["Key Matrix (K = X * Wk)"]
    Input --> V["Value Matrix (V = X * Wv)"]
    Q --> Dot["Dot Product (Q · K^T)"]
    K --> Dot
    Dot --> Scale["Scale by 1/sqrt(d_k)"]
    Scale --> Softmax["Softmax (Attention Weights)"]
    Softmax --> WeightedSum["Weighted Sum with V"]
    V --> WeightedSum
    WeightedSum --> Output["Contextual Output Z"]
    style Softmax fill:#6366f1,stroke:#4338ca,color:#fff
    style WeightedSum fill:#10b981,stroke:#047857,color:#fff
visualAction.explanationNotes: Notice how Q acts as a search query, K acts as file tags, and V represents the actual content.

checkpoint.questionText: Why do we compute the dot product between the Query vector and Key vector in self-attention?

options.text: To measure the semantic compatibility or relevance between two tokens.
options.feedback: Spot on! The dot product measures alignment in embedding space.

options.text: To reduce the dimension of the embeddings to save memory.
options.feedback: Dot product produces a scalar similarity score, not a dimension reduction technique.

options.text: To introduce non-linear activation functions into the network.
options.feedback: Dot product is a linear operation; Softmax provides the normalization.

options.text: To randomly drop tokens during training.
options.feedback: That would be dropout, not Query-Key dot products.

checkpoint.expectedConcept: The dot product of Query and Key calculates similarity or attention weights between pairs of words.
checkpoint.rubric: Check that student recognizes dot product as a measure of token-to-token similarity or relevance.

modules.title: The Scaled Dot-Product Equation
modules.teachingScript: <emotion=thoughtful>Ab aate hain exact mathematical formulation par. <pause=400ms> Dekho formula bohot elegant hai: Attention of Q, K, V is Softmax of Q times K transpose divided by root d_k, multiplied by V. <emotion=curious>Lekin yahan root d_k se divide kyu karte hain?</emotion> Kyunki jab vectors bade hote hain, dot product bahut bada ho jata hai, aur Softmax gradients zero ho jate hain!</emotion>

visualAction.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Equation
visualAction.explanationNotes: d_k is the dimension of the key vectors. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) stabilizes gradient flow during backpropagation.

checkpoint.questionText: What would happen if we omitted the 1 / sqrt(d_k) scaling factor when d_k is large (e.g. 512)?
checkpoint.expectedConcept: Large dot product values cause softmax outputs to saturate at 0 or 1, leading to extremely small (vanishing) gradients.
checkpoint.rubric: Look for mention of softmax saturation, large variance in dot products, or vanishing gradients during backpropagation.

modules.title: PyTorch Implementation in Action
modules.teachingScript: <emotion=encouraging>Let's turn this theory into code! Here is how we implement Single-Head Attention cleanly in PyTorch in just a few lines of matrix operations.</emotion>

visualAction.title: ScaledDotProductAttention.py
visualAction.rawPayload:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class ScaledDotProductAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_k: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.scale = 1.0 / (d_k ** 0.5)

    def forward(self, Q, K, V, mask=None):
        # Q, K, V: [batch, seq_len, d_k]
        scores = torch.matmul(Q, K.transpose(-2, -1)) * self.scale
        if mask is not None:
            scores = scores.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)
        attn_weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        output = torch.matmul(attn_weights, V)
        return output, attn_weights
visualAction.explanationNotes: Notice the transpose of K on line 11 and the masked_fill for autoregressive decoding on line 13.

checkpoint.questionText: In decoder self-attention, what is the purpose of the mask on line 13?

options.text: To prevent the model from attending to subsequent future tokens during autoregressive generation.
options.feedback: Correct! Causal masking ensures causality in language generation.
Softmax naturally bounds weights between 0 and 1, so negative weights don't exist.

options.text: To speed up matrix multiplication by 50%.
options.feedback: Masking doesn't speed up compute unless specialized sparse kernels are used.

checkpoint.expectedConcept: Causal mask prevents attention to future tokens during generative decoding.
checkpoint.rubric: Verify understanding of autoregressive causal masking.
